items.a: No — and we won't say it is. The change history is tamper-evident: it reveals that a record was altered after the fact; it does not prevent alteration. The weak link is never the record, it's the people using it — and we say so plainly.

items.q: Who owns the account — the owner or the builder?
items.a: Whoever holds the subscription — it can be either side. But paying for the account never means owning the record against the other: the platform stays the neutral ground both work from.

items.q: I run several builds. Can I manage them all here?
items.a: Yes — LinkNMS is multi-build by design. You switch between your builds and see them all in one portfolio dashboard: budget health, schedule and pending approvals per build. What it is not is your back office — no accounting, payroll or CRM.

items.q: Can I bring in my BIM model?
items.a: Yes — LinkNMS is designed to let you upload and preview the project's model and submit it as the build's BIM record, attached to the history. It is not a modelling tool: it doesn't author, edit, or run clash detection.

items.q: Does it work on my phone?
items.a: It's built phone-first. The people entering and checking the record are on site, with a phone in hand — so that's the primary way to use it.

argument.headline: You said this cost {quote}.
argument.sub: Nobody is lying. The kitchen moved, the tiles were swapped, the frame slipped two weeks. It all happened in WhatsApp, on site, over the phone — and none of it is written down anywhere both sides can read.

planIn.headline: Upload what you already have.
planIn.sub: Nobody rebuilds their budget from scratch. Drop in the spreadsheet you quoted with and linkNMS reads it into work packages, sub-tasks and prices.

01.d: XLSX, CSV or PDF. Straight from the estimator, no template to fill.

02.d: You map price, quantity and dates once. It remembers your format.

planIn.tableCaption: The uploaded spreadsheet, parsed into work packages and sub-tasks.
planIn.band: No spreadsheet? Specialty partners build the plan inside linkNMS and export it. The plan always belongs to whoever does the work — and the acceptance proof is identical either way.

materials.label: Materials & money
materials.headline: Half the budget is a material decision.
materials.body: Wood or tile. Brick, or concrete with ETICS. Each line of the plan carries the materials it rests on, with quantities and unit prices. Swap one and the overview redraws itself — you see exactly which slice of the budget moved, by how much, and who signed it off.
materials.body2: When a supplier raises the price of brick in March, that is not a change order. It is a price movement, and linkNMS records it as its own kind of event.
